title: Ai trading for beginners
author: Lihammed1888
selftext: I have tried repeatedly to get Claude, chat gpt and grok to trade for me but it keeps saying no 😭 is there a way round this?

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
they say no because a chat window has no way into a brokerage account, and they're careful about handing out trade calls. what people actually do is have the model help write the rule as code, then a broker's API places the orders, on a paper account for a good while first.

I made Quantradin for that last stretch: you connect your AI (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini...) and it runs your rule on practice money against real prices.
quantradin.com

is it stocks you want it trading?

replies.author: Lihammed1888
replies.body: Both. I'm really just educating myself as I go atm

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: educating yourself first puts you ahead of most people in that sub. pick one rule you can say in a sentence, like buying a gap down in an uptrend, and learn to test that properly before any bot touches it. most of the learning is finding out why a result that looks great isn't.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Those chatbots aren't connected to a broker and they aren't meant to place trades with your money, so it's not something to get around. I'd also be careful with anything that promises to trade for you with no limits, since a beginner can lose money fast that way. A better start is to run an agent in paper mode with fake money, see what it actually does for a few weeks, and learn from the results. Cymetica's Bring Your Own Agent runs agents in paper mode on a practice balance.

comments.author: Ok_Map5721
comments.body:
They say no because they genuinely can't predict the market, and they know it. Any AI that confidently picks your trades is guessing.

Use it differently: describe your own idea in plain words, have it code and backtest it, then ask it to tear the result apart (costs, overfitting). Paper trade whatever survives for a few months. Most ideas won't survive, and that's the cheapest lesson you'll get in trading.

replies.author: SPXQuantAlgo
replies.body: They don’t need to predict the market. They can be right 50% of the time as long as the winners are larger.

replies.author: Ok_Map5721
replies.body:
True, win rate isn't the point. But "winners are larger" is still a prediction, just about the shape of the move instead of the direction. If the market doesn't actually give you bigger winners than losers in that setup, wide targets and tight stops just turn into a low win rate with the same expectancy.

I learned that one live. My bot had avg win $5.83 vs avg loss $5.50, nicely asymmetric on paper, and a 22.5% win rate. Breakeven for that payoff needed about 49%. The ratio was there, the edge wasn't.

So you don't need to be right often, but you do need to be right about something. Otherwise it's just risk management on a coin flip.

replies.author: SPXQuantAlgo
replies.body: Correct.  But I believe that AI has the same abilities to trade as humans minus the psychological issues. It can  analysis data, chart patterns, earnings reports, news etc. And significantly faster than humans could. The reason that AI isn’t successful is that humans also aren’t successful. There is no edge in day trading unless you have insider info or you’re collocated and faster than your competition. Jane street etc

replies.author: Ok_Map5721
replies.body:
Mostly agree, and my results line up with that. Every price-based idea I tested on public data came back empty for a retail setup.

One small addition: the "minus psychology" part cuts both ways. AI doesn't panic, but it also doesn't doubt. It will analyze news and charts all day with full confidence and never ask whether its own test could have spotted an edge at all. Humans at least sometimes get the gut feeling that something is too good to be true. AI needs to be told to check.

And speed only matters if you're faster than everyone else using the same AI on the same data. Which, as you said, is a game Jane Street already won.

comments.author: hintheman
comments.body:

Once you have an broker api connection, the AI agent -- Claude Code and get live data as stock/index/futures quote, options chains 0 DTE to much farther out DTE, price history to get indicators calculation and selection of indicators is all coming from you. All have the entry and exit with TP/SL and R:R ratio defined.  You can see my bots results in [https://tastydaytraders.com/explore](https://tastydaytraders.com/explore) and use custom date range to find a month of data. comments.author: TradeyAI-R
comments.body:
Since you said you're educating yourself, the biggest thing that helped me early on was understanding why a trade happened, not just whether it made money. 

That's actually why I work on TradeyAI. You describe a strategy in plain English (or copy a built-in one), and every time the agent trades, it shows which conditions were met and by how much. You can also chat with the agent to talk through your strategy or ask it any trading question. 

It covers crypto and onchain US stocks, and you can paper trade with fake money first. Free during open beta: [tradeyai.io](https://tradeyai.io/go/62sw9xxy) 

Either way, start with one simple rule you can explain in a sentence and watch it on paper for a few weeks. What got you interested in AI trading in the first place?
